prompt: What makes a passkey more phishing-resistant than a one-time code sent by SMS?
explanation: Passkeys are origin-bound key pairs — the authentication happens with the genuine site, so a look-alike phishing page gets nothing usable. SMS codes can be relayed or intercepted; that is the gap passkeys close.

options.text: It is a cryptographic credential bound to the device and the real GitHub domain, so a fake site cannot capture it
It is longer than six digits
It changes every 30 seconds, unlike SMS codes
It is stored in the browser’s cache
